title:
I could easily catch hold of her when she comes up to my step: nobody is looking. I could hold her and kiss her.
 
 But he did neither:
html_source:
Symbolizes young love and the insecurities and limitations you feel as you’re coming of age. This interaction is an important indicator of Stephen’s interactions with women throughout the novel and his ability to become unnerved and self-reflective in the presence of women.
Questions that arise: Why didn’t Stephen just kiss her if he felt a reciprocated emotion? Did he not feel good enough?

Too bad Sebastian from the Little Mermaid wasn’t at the tram station singing his usual words of encouragement “Dont be scared. You got the mood prepared. Go on and kiss the girl…”

I could easily catch hold of her when she comes up to my step: nobody is looking. I could hold her and kiss her.
 
 But he did neither:
anchor.prefix:
stood listlessly in his place, seemingly a tranquil watcher of the scene before him.

 —She too wants me to catch hold of her, he thought. That’s why she came with me to the tram.
anchor.suffix:
